messages.author: 889de486273d901d
messages.subject: Re: problems with runGist
parts:
Julin, 

I suspect your problem with runGist is caused by an out-of-date or missing SSL certificate for github.com on your machine.
You can confirm this by observing the output of this command, 

> shiny:::download("https://gist.github.com/3239667/download", "temp")
--2013-09-21 14:07:44--  https://gist.github.com/3239667/download
Resolving gist.github.com... 192.30.252.142
Connecting to gist.github.com|192.30.252.142|:443... connected.
ERROR: cannot verify gist.github.com's certificate, issued by `/C=US/O=DigiCert Inc/OU=www.digicert.com/CN=DigiCert High Assurance CA-3':
  Unable to locally verify the issuer's authority.
To connect to gist.github.com insecurely, use `--no-check-certificate'.
Unable to establish SSL connection.

Warning message:
In download.file(url, method = method, ...) :
  download had nonzero exit status

If you get an error message similar to the one above you can fix this a couple of ways -- You could go get a current ssl certificate for github (I don't know how to do that),  or you can tell the download tool to no check the certificate.   On my MacOS system I do that with the following command:

> options("download.file.extra" = "--no-check-certificate")

That's it.   If you want this to be a permanent change in your R environment you will want to put this command in your .rprofile file.
